title: Negotiator pocket: clauses, escalation & walkaways
content:
Purpose: super-compact personal reference for fast redlines and live negotiation. Not a substitute for Legal sign-off — use for call prep and flagging.

Top-level risk categories (quick):
- High risk (escalate immediately): unlimited indemnity to vendor, open-ended data processing for customer PII, broad audit rights without scope, vendor liability without cap, exclusive long-term lock-in clauses.
- Medium risk (push back / trade): carveouts for third-party IP claims, high SLA credits that assume vendor fault, broad subcontractor/subprocessor language without notification.
- Low risk (accept / monitor): standard confidentiality, short-term pilot terms, non-material IP license grants for customer-provided data.

Clause-by-clause cheat notes (my shorthand + proposed fallback language):
1) Indemnity
- Flag: mutual vs one-way, third-party IP claims where vendor indemnifies customer for model outputs is risky.
- Talking points: "We need indemnity tied to vendor's negligence or breach — can't accept indemnity for customer's configuration or prompt misuse."
- Fallback redline snippet: "Vendor will indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims to the extent arising from Vendor's Models or services, provided Customer's use is in accordance with the Agreement and Vendor's documentation."

2) Data responsibility / processing
- Flag: vendor trying to treat customer data as its own or blanket rights to use for improvements.
- Talking points: "Customer data (including prompts & outputs) remains Customer data; vendor may process for service delivery, and only use for product improvement with explicit opt-in and appropriate anonymization."
- Fallback: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train models or improve model weights without Customer's prior written consent. Vendor may use aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry for service quality improvements."

3) IP & outputs
- Flag: vendor claiming ownership of customer outputs or derivative rights.
- Talking points: "Customer needs ownership or an unlimited license to outputs for product use; vendor can claim model weights as its IP but not outputs."
- Fallback: "Customer retains all rights in Customer Data and Outputs. Vendor retains rights in Models and underlying software but grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive license to Outputs necessary for Customer's business."

4) Limitation of Liability (LoL) & caps
- Flag: cap that excludes direct damages or has very low multiple of fees; carveouts for confidentiality and IP should be uncapped or higher.
- Talking points: "We accept a commercially reasonable cap tied to fees in year, with standard exceptions for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, and IP indemnity."
- Fallback: "Liability shall be limited to the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (b) $1,000,000, except for liability arising from breach of confidentiality, IP infringement, or gross negligence, which are not subject to the cap."

5) Termination & migration assistance
- Flag: no requirement for data return/secure deletion or no migration assistance on termination.
- Talking points: "On termination for convenience or breach, Customer must get copies of its data and a reasonable migration period plus assistance."
- Fallback: "Upon termination, Vendor will export Customer Data in a common format and provide 30 days of migration assistance at no charge."

6) Security & breach notifications
- Flag: slow notification windows (30+ days), vague remediation obligations.
- Talking points: "Need 72-hour initial notification for security incidents affecting Customer Data and clear remediation timelines."
- Fallback: "Vendor will notify Customer within 72 hours of detection of a security incident affecting Customer Data and provide regular updates until remediation."

7) Subprocessors / subcontractors
- Flag: broad right to engage any subprocessor without notice or objection.
- Talking points: "Require notice and right to object for sensitive subprocessors; must flow down security obligations."
- Fallback: "Vendor will provide a list of subprocessors and notify Customer of material changes; Customer may reasonably object to a new subprocessor."

8) Audit rights
- Flag: customer gets unlimited onsite audits without scope limits, or vendor demands audits only at customer's cost.
- Talking points: "We need scoped evidence of controls, preferably SOC2 report plus limited remote evidence; avoid frequent in-person audits for hosted SaaS."
- Fallback: "Customer may request relevant compliance reports (SOC2, ISO) annually; any on-site audit shall be limited in frequency and scope and subject to confidentiality and cost-sharing if excessive."

9) SLA & credits
- Flag: credits that are low or require claim windows that are too small, or SLA that excludes model degradation.
- Talking points: "SLA should cover platform availability; model quality regressions should trigger rollback/fallback commitments in rollouts."
- Fallback: "Availability target 99.9% monthly; credits are proportionate and cumulative, and must be claimable within 60 days."

Negotiation scripts (short):
- For IP ownership: "We can accept that you keep model IP. However, outputs derived from our data must remain ours. If you need usage data to improve models, let's scope it to aggregated non-attributable telemetry or opt-in program with compensatory terms."
- For LoL: "We can meet you halfway on cap — tie it to ARR paid in the last 12 months. But carve out IP indemnity and confidentiality from the cap."
- For data-use-for-improvements: "Can we agree on an opt-in checkbox and a data processing addendum that limits training use and requires anonymization?"

Escalation triggers (call out quick):
- Any clause that converts vendor to data controller for Customer PII.
- Vendor wants ownership or unrestricted use of Customer Outputs.
- Vendor requests uncapped indemnity in favor of vendor (rare but watch).
- New or nonstandard export control language affecting our ability to serve global customers.

Personal favorites / quick concessions I'm willing to make on calls:
- Accept standard mutual NDA language and basic support SLAs if core risk mitigated.
- Allow limited telemetry for monitoring (uptime, error rates) without deep content collection.
- Agree to template subprocessor list update cadence rather than prior consent in low-risk cases.

Unresolved items / TODOs for Legal review before sending to Sales:
- Ask infra team whether 30-day migration window is technically feasible for on-prem snapshots (JIRA:INFRA-789).
- Confirm acceptable numeric cap floor with Finance (propose $1M minimum).
- Get SOC2 attestation copy from Vendor as pre-sig requirement.

Notes to self (call prep checklist):
- Print this sheet, highlight IP, indemnity, and data-use lines.
- Prepare two fallback paragraphs: one aggressive (for enterprise deals) and one pragmatic (for pilot/proof-of-concept).
- Slack draft to #legal-negotiations with proposed redline before sending final to counterparty.

Examples of short redline language (copy/paste-ready):
- Data use limited: "Vendor will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or enhance any model weights or architectures without Customer's separate prior written consent."
- Export of data: "All Customer Data will be stored and processed only in the regions agreed in Appendix A unless Customer consents otherwise in writing."

Quick references:
- Confluence playbook link (main): https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/LEGAL/Contract+Playbook
- Slack history: #legal-negotiations has templates and past concessions — search "training opt-in"

Bottom line: primary goals are protect Customer Data/Outputs, preserve customer IP rights, keep vendor liability tethered to commercial fees, and require practical notice/assistance obligations on security and termination. Use this as live notes in calls and escalate high-risk flags to Legal+Finance.

----
Personal log: got pressured once on "training clause" during demo deal — vendor offered credit in return. If confident about data residency and anonymization, opt-in with explicit compensation and timebound scope.

End of pocket notes.
